hook: Four lads from Liverpool who became the best-selling band in history.

pages.x: In 1957, at a church fair in Liverpool, 15-year-old Paul McCartney met 16-year-old John Lennon, who led a skiffle band. Paul joined, and soon brought in his young friend George Harrison.
From 1960 they played long nights in rough clubs in Hamburg, Germany, sometimes for hours on end, and turned into a tight, tireless live band.
Back home they played nearly 300 times at the Cavern Club in Liverpool. Brian Epstein became their manager, and in 1962 Ringo Starr became their drummer.

pages.t: I Want to Hold Your Hand
pages.x: In 1963 Beatlemania swept Britain: screaming fans, mop-top haircuts and sold-out shows. This song became their first number one in America.
In February 1964 some 73 million Americans watched them on The Ed Sullivan Show. By April they held the top five places in the American singles chart.

Paul woke up one morning with this melody in his head, and for weeks played it to friends, sure he must have heard it somewhere. Until he wrote the real words, he sang it about scrambled eggs. It is one of the most recorded songs ever.
Fans screamed so loudly that the band could not hear themselves play. After a last concert in San Francisco in 1966, they gave up touring to work in the studio.
In 1967 they released Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band, full of studio tricks, orchestras and the sounds of Indian music. It is often called the greatest album ever made.

pages.x: In 1968 they travelled to Rishikesh, in India, to learn meditation, and wrote dozens of new songs there.
Paul wrote it to comfort John's young son, Julian, when his parents split up. More than seven minutes long, it spent nine weeks at number one in America.

In January 1969 they played their last show, on the roof of their London office, until the police came. The cover of Abbey Road shows them walking over the zebra crossing outside their studio. They split up in 1970.
The Beatles are the best-selling band in history. They wrote their own songs, changed pop music, and turned the recording studio into an instrument.
